question: A 42-year-old man comes to the physician for 1 month of worsening right knee pain. He has not had any trauma other than stubbing his toe 3 days ago at the garage where he works as a mechanic. Examination of the right knee shows swelling and erythema with fluctuance over the inferior patella. There is tenderness on palpation of the patella but no joint line tenderness or warmth. The range of flexion is limited because of the pain. Which of the following is the most likely underlying cause of this patient's symptoms?

options.opd: Deposition of crystals in the joint

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Worsening right knee pain" -> "Swelling and erythema over the inferior patella" -> "Fluctuance over the inferior patella" -> "Tenderness on palpation of the patella" -> "Limited range of flexion due to pain" -> "Infection of the joint" -> 80% CHAIN: "Worsening right knee pain" -> "Swelling and erythema over the inferior patella" -> "Fluctuance over the inferior patella" -> "Tenderness on palpation of the patella" -> "Limited range of flexion due to pain" -> "Inflammation of periarticular fluid-filled sac" -> 80%
analysis: Based on the clinical presentation of swelling, erythema, fluctuance, tenderness on palpation of the patella, and limited range of flexion, the most likely underlying cause of this patient's symptoms is an infection of the joint.
